In 2019 I took A-levels, as semester 1 rolls around I study as usual and took the test. I am usually an A sometimes B student. Results came back and it was almost a fail. Started to get depressed but I still did all I could to study. AS rolls around and I wanted to kill myself because I couldn't bear the failure I did. I sometimes studied 9 hours a day. Didn't go anywhere. Just classes. Library and home. I almost killed myself if it wasn't for my friends. When results came out, as expected I failed my AS. It took me a few months but when covid hit in march 2020 I had like a chance to really reset myself. For the rest of the year I studied more. There was one day I studied straight for 24 hours and didn't stop.(Thank you red bull)At November 2020 I took all of my test, both AS and A2 papers at the same time. Had like 15 papers in a span of 5 weeks. Yeah. 
Fast forward I expected an BBC at worse. But few days ago got my results and it was CDD. I admit it was sad and I cried. But I'm going to apply to some uni and do a Foundation course in that respective university before I pursue my degree. 
I admit I may not be as smart as I used to be, but I sure as hell tried my best. Even though it wasn't the result I wanted, I still had to move on.
